questions.question: The dissolution of which of the following in water makes the solution acidic due to the formation of sulphurous acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sulphur dioxide** (SO₂) is a gaseous **non-metal oxide** that exhibits acidic properties when dissolved in water.
 
• The chemical reaction between **Sulphur dioxide** and **water** (H₂O) results in the formation of **sulphurous acid** (H₂SO₃).
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this process is: **SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃**.
 
• **Sulphurous acid** is a weak, unstable **dibasic acid** that increases the concentration of **hydrogen ions** in the solution, thereby lowering the pH and making it **acidic**.
 
• This chemical interaction is a primary mechanism behind the formation of **acid rain**, where industrial SO₂ emissions react with atmospheric moisture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sulphur trioxide (SO₃)**:

 
 
• It reacts violently with water to form **sulphuric acid** (H₂SO₄), which is a much stronger acid than sulphurous acid.
 
• It is the primary precursor for the industrial production of **concentrated sulphuric acid** via the **Contact Process**.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur hexafluoride (SF₆)**:
 
 
• It is a colorless, odorless, and inorganic gas known for being chemically **inert** and highly stable.
 
• Due to its excellent **dielectric properties**, it is widely used as an **electrical insulator** in high-voltage circuit breakers and transformers.
 
 
 
• **Sulphonic acid**:
 
 
• This refers to a class of **organosulfur compounds** containing the functional group −SO₃H.
 
• They are fundamentally different from sulphurous acid and are extensively used in the manufacturing of **synthetic detergents**, dyes, and drugs like **sulfa antibiotics**.

questions.question: As mentioned in the Economic Survey 2024-25, what was the diaspora population of India in 2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**18 million**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Economic Survey 2024-25**, India continues to have the largest **transnational population** in the world, which serves as a significant source of **human capital** and economic support.
 
• As of **2020**, the size of the **Indian diaspora** was estimated at **18 million**, based on data provided by the **United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)** in its **International Migration** reports.
 
• The **diaspora** includes **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)** and **Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs)** who reside across nearly every continent, with high concentrations in the **United Arab Emirates**, the **United States**, and **Saudi Arabia**.
 
• This massive population base is the primary reason why India remains the top recipient of **inward remittances** globally, which helps maintain the country's **Current Account Balance** and foreign exchange reserves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Economic Contributions**:

 
 
• India's **remittance inflows** reached a milestone of **USD 125 billion** in 2023, supported by the diverse skill sets of the **18 million** migrants ranging from **high-tech professionals** to **semi-skilled workers**.
 
• The **World Bank** reports highlight that the **United States** has surpassed the **Gulf regions** as the single largest source of these remittances for India in recent years.

• The **Government of India** engages with this population through the **Ministry of External Affairs** and initiatives like the **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**, celebrated on **January 9** to mark **Mahatma Gandhi’s** return to India.
 
• Global rankings in **2020** placed **Mexico** and **Russia** significantly behind India, with each having roughly 11 million citizens living abroad.

questions.question: The Arms Act of 1878 was introduced during the tenure of which Viceroy of British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Lytton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Lytton** served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1876 to 1880**, a period marked by several controversial and reactionary policies.
 
• The **Indian Arms Act (Act XI of 1878)** was enacted to prevent Indians from keeping, bearing, or trafficking in arms without a specific **license**.
 
• A primary feature of the act was its **racial discrimination**; it exempted **Europeans**, **Anglo-Indians**, and certain government officials from the requirement of a license, while making it mandatory for native Indians.
 
• The act categorized the possession of unlicensed weapons by Indians as a **criminal offense**, punishable by fines or **imprisonment**.
 
• This legislation was part of a broader strategy to disarm the Indian population and prevent any potential repeat of the **1857 Uprising**.
 
• Alongside the Arms Act, Lytton also introduced the **Vernacular Press Act of 1878** to silence criticism of the British administration in local Indian languages.
 
• His tenure also witnessed the **Royal Titles Act of 1876**, which proclaimed **Queen Victoria** as the **Empress of India (Kaiser-i-Hind)** at the first **Delhi Durbar** in **1877**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Ripon (1880-1884)**:

 
 
• Known for his liberal reforms, he repealed the **Vernacular Press Act** in **1882**.
 
• He is regarded as the **Father of Local Self-Government** in India due to his **1882 Resolution**.
 
• The **Ilbert Bill** controversy occurred during his term, which aimed to allow Indian magistrates to try Europeans.
 
 
 
• **Lord Curzon (1899-1905)**:
 
 
• Famous for the **Partition of Bengal** in **1905**, which led to the **Swadeshi Movement**.
 
• He established the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** through the **Ancient Monuments Preservation Act of 1904**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley (1798-1805)**:
 
 
• He introduced the **Subsidiary Alliance** system to bring Indian princely states under British control.
 
• He founded the **Fort William College** at **Calcutta** in **1800** to train British civil servants in Indian languages and customs.

questions.question: Diabetes, cancer, and asthma are collectively known as which type of disorders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-communicable diseases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Non-communicable diseases (NCDs)**, also known as **chronic diseases**, are medical conditions that are not transmissible directly from one person to another.
 
• These diseases generally have a **slow progression** and a long duration, often requiring long-term management rather than a quick cure.
 
• **Diabetes** is a metabolic NCD characterized by high blood sugar levels resulting from the body's inability to produce or use **insulin** effectively.
 
• **Cancer** refers to a large group of diseases that can start in almost any organ or tissue when abnormal cells grow uncontrollably, go beyond their usual boundaries, and spread to other organs.
 
• **Asthma** is a chronic condition affecting the **respiratory system**, characterized by inflammation and narrowing of the **bronchial tubes**, which leads to difficulty in breathing and wheezing.
 
• According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, NCDs are the leading cause of death globally, often linked to common risk factors such as tobacco use, physical inactivity, unhealthy diets, and harmful use of alcohol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Communicable diseases**:

 
 
• These are **infectious diseases** caused by **pathogens** like bacteria, viruses, parasites, or fungi.
 
• Examples include **Tuberculosis**, **Malaria**, and **COVID-19**, which can spread through air, water, or bodily fluids.
 
 
 
• **Deficiency diseases**:
 
 
• These occur when the body lacks **essential nutrients**, vitamins, or minerals over a prolonged period.
 
• Common examples include **Scurvy** (Vitamin C deficiency) and **Goitre** (Iodine deficiency).
 
 
 
• **Airborne diseases**:
 
 
• This is a specific category of communicable diseases where **microorganisms** are transmitted through small droplets or particles suspended in the **atmosphere**.

questions.question: Which of the following was a major military reason behind the construction of Siri Fort?

options.text: To serve as a trading hub for the Songara Rajputs
To celebrate Khilji's victory over the Cholas
To protect Delhi from Mongol attacks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To protect Delhi from Mongol attacks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Siri Fort** was built by **Sultan Alauddin Khilji**, the second ruler of the **Khilji Dynasty**, around **1303 AD** as the second city of **Delhi**.
 
• The primary military objective for its construction was to safeguard the **Delhi Sultanate** from the persistent threat of **Mongol invasions** originating from the **Chagatai Khanate**.
 
• Following a massive Mongol siege led by **Targhi** in **1303**, which highlighted the vulnerability of the existing capital at **Lalkot**, Alauddin Khilji recognized the need for a heavily fortified **garrison town**.
 
• The fort was designed to house a massive **permanent standing army** and provide a secure defensive perimeter against the swift cavalry tactics of the Mongol forces.
 
• It featured high walls, circular bastions, and advanced defensive architecture, making it the first city of Delhi built entirely by a Muslim ruler for purely strategic and **military purposes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alauddin Khilji**:

 
 
• He was known for his administrative and military reforms, including the **Dagh** (branding of horses) and **Chehra** (descriptive roll of soldiers) systems to combat corruption.
 
• He adopted the title **Sikandar-i-Sani** (Alexander the Second), reflecting his ambitions for world conquest and his successful defense against multiple Mongol incursions.
 
 
 
• **Hauz-i-Alai**:
 
 
• To ensure a reliable water supply for the **Siri** garrison and the city's inhabitants during prolonged sieges, the Sultan excavated a massive reservoir known as **Hauz-i-Alai**, which is today known as **Hauz Khas**.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Defense**:
 
 
• The construction of Siri was part of a broader defensive strategy that included the repair of old forts and the construction of new outposts along the **North-West Frontier** of India to intercept Mongol raiders before they reached the heart of the **Sultanate**.

questions.question: Which mountain range lies immediately to the south of the Vindhyan Range, separated by the Narmada Valley?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satpura Range**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Satpura Range** is a prominent series of seven hills located in **Central India**, stretching in a roughly east-west direction parallel to the **Vindhyan Range**.
 
• The **Narmada Valley** acts as a structural **Rift Valley** that geographically separates the **Vindhyan Range** to the north from the **Satpura Range** to the south.
 
• The **Narmada River**, which originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau**, flows westward through this deep valley between the two mountain ranges before emptying into the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The **Satpura Range** serves as a critical watershed between the **Narmada River** basin to its north and the **Tapi River** basin to its south.
 
• The highest peak of the **Satpura Range** is **Dhupgarh**, reaching an elevation of **1,350 meters**, situated near the hill station of **Pachmarhi** in **Madhya Pradesh**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vindhyan Range**:

 
 
• It is a complex and discontinuous chain of mountain ridges that forms the southern edge of the **Malwa Plateau** and the northern wall of the **Narmada Valley**.
 
• The range is primarily composed of **Sedimentary Rocks** such as **Sandstone**, **Shales**, and **Limestones**, and it marks the traditional boundary between **Northern India** and the **Deccan**.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range**:
 
 
• Located in northwestern India, it extends from **Gujarat** through **Rajasthan** to **Haryana** and **Delhi**.
 
• It is recognized as one of the world's oldest **Fold Mountain** systems, with **Guru Shikhar** being its highest peak.
 
 
 
• **Western Ghats**:
 
 
• Also known as **Sahyadri**, this range runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula for nearly 1,600 kilometers.
 
• It is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and is one of the eight hottest **Biodiversity Hotspots** in the world.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats**:
 
 
• A discontinuous and lower-altitude range of hills along India's eastern coast, eroded by major rivers like the **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri**.
 
• The range meets the **Western Ghats** at the **Nilgiri Hills** in the south.

questions.question: Which combination correctly matches the device with its primary function?

options.text: OMR – Detecting shaded marks on paper

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**OMR - Detecting shaded marks on paper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Optical Mark Recognition (OMR)**: This technology is specifically designed to detect the presence or absence of a mark on a specific document location. It is widely utilized for processing **Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs)** and surveys, where a scanner reflects light onto the paper to identify shaded regions. ***Hence, OMR matches with Detecting shaded marks on paper.***
 
• **Optical Character Recognition (OCR)**: This device identifies individual letters and symbols from printed or handwritten documents, transforming them into digital, editable text. It does not primarily use magnetic ink. ***Hence, OCR matches with Converting printed or handwritten text into digital data.***
 
• **Magnetic Ink Character Recognition (MICR)**: This is a specialized technology used by banks to read the **MICR code** printed at the bottom of checks using magnetic ink. It is not designed for barcode scanning. ***Hence, MICR matches with Recognizing magnetic ink characters.***
 
• **Barcode Reader**: This is an optical scanner that interprets the light reflected from a series of black-and-white vertical lines (barcodes) to retrieve product information. It is not used for capturing handwriting. ***Hence, Barcode Reader matches with Reading barcodes.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OMR Systems**:

 
 
• These systems are highly efficient for high-volume data collection and are valued for their **99.9% accuracy** in reading standardized forms.
 
• Common applications include **competitive exam OMR sheets**, voting ballots, and demographic surveys.
 
 
 
• **OCR Technology**:
 
 
• Modern **OCR software** utilizes **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Machine Learning (ML)** to improve character recognition across different fonts and languages.
 
• It is vital for the **digitization** of historical archives and automated data entry in offices.
 
 
 
• **MICR Features**:
 
 
• The **MICR line** typically contains the check number, **9-digit routing number**, and account number.
 
• It provides a high level of security as the magnetic ink is difficult to forge and can be read even if the check is folded or smudged.
 
 
 
• **Barcode Scanning**:
 
 
• Barcodes follow international standards like **UPC (Universal Product Code)** and **EAN (European Article Number)**.
 
• The reader uses a **laser beam** or an **LED** to capture the varying reflectance of the black bars and white spaces.

questions.question: When using the search term Invoice* in Windows 11 File Explorer, which files will be found?

options.text: Files that begin with the word “Invoice”
Files that have “Invoice” anywhere in the name
Files that contain exactly the word “Invoice”
Files that end with the word “Invoice”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Files that begin with the word 'Invoice'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Windows 11 File Explorer**, the **asterisk (*)** is a fundamental **wildcard character** that represents any number of characters, including zero characters, within a filename or extension.
 
• When a user appends the asterisk to a string, such as **Invoice***, it signals a **prefix search**, instructing the **Windows Search Indexer** to locate all files and folders that commence with that specific sequence of letters.
 
• This search query will effectively return files like **Invoice_July.pdf**, **Invoices.docx**, or **Invoice1.txt** because they all satisfy the condition of starting with the designated term.
 
• The use of this wildcard is distinct from a suffix search (e.g., ***Invoice**) or a 'contains' search (e.g., ***Invoice***), as the **prefix condition** strictly mandates that the word **Invoice** must appear at the very beginning of the filename.
 
• In the absence of a wildcard, modern **File Explorer** searches often default to finding the term as a whole word or a word start anywhere in the name, but the explicit trailing asterisk reinforces the **starts-with** logic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Question Mark (?) Wildcard**

 
 
• This character acts as a placeholder for exactly **one** character.
 
• For instance, a search for **Invoice?** would find **Invoice1** or **InvoiceA**, but would not return **Invoice12**.
 
 
 
• **Advanced Query Syntax (AQS)**
 
 
• **Microsoft** employs **AQS** to allow users to refine results using specific properties like **kind:**, **size:**, or **ext:**.
 
• Using **Invoice* ext:.pdf** would further narrow results to only **PDF** documents starting with the word **Invoice**.
 
 
 
• **Case Sensitivity**
 
 
• **Windows File Explorer** is **case-insensitive** by design, meaning the search **Invoice*** will match **invoice_report.xlsx** as well as **INVOICE_REPORT.xlsx**.

questions.question: The International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women marks the beginning of which global campaign?

options.text: 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women** is observed globally on **November 25** every year.
 
• This day serves as the starting point for the **16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence**, a global campaign that runs until **December 10**, which is **Human Rights Day**.
 
• The campaign was originated by activists at the first **Women's Global Leadership Institute** in **1991** and continues to be coordinated each year by the **Center for Women's Global Leadership (CWGL)**.
 
• The choice of **November 25** commemorates the **Mirabal sisters**, three political activists from the **Dominican Republic** who were brutally assassinated in **1960** by order of the country's dictator, **Rafael Trujillo**.
 
• The symbolic conclusion of the campaign on **December 10** emphasizes that violence against women is a fundamental violation of **human rights**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNiTE by 2030 to End Violence against Women Campaign**:

 
 
• Launched in **2008** by the **United Nations Secretary-General**, this initiative supports the **16 Days of Activism** through global advocacy and social mobilization.
 
• The campaign uses **Orange** as its signature color, representing a brighter future and a world free from violence against women and girls.
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly** officially designated **November 25** as the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women through **Resolution 54/134** in **1999**.
 
 
 
• **Human Rights Day (December 10)**:
 
 
• This day honors the date the **United Nations General Assembly** adopted the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR)** in **1948**.
 
• It serves as the terminal date for the activism period to highlight that women's rights are integral, indivisible, and universal human rights.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme is INCORRECT?

options.text: The program started with the launch of Palakkad-Bangalore-Mumbai-Ahmedabad Industrial Corridor in 2010
It seeks to develop new industrial cities as smart cities by integrating next-generation technologies across infrastructure sectors
It aims at providing complete “plug and play” infrastructure till the plot level along with building sustainable future ready cities

• The **National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP)** actually began with the conceptualization of the **Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)** following a **Memorandum of Understanding** signed between the **Government of India** and the **Government of Japan** in **December 2006**, with project approval occurring in **2007**. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• The program is designed to develop **Greenfield Industrial Cities** as **Smart Cities** by leveraging **Next-Generation Technologies** like **ICT-enabled infrastructure**, **SCADA** systems, and **Integrated Command and Control Centers (ICCC)**. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• A primary objective is the provision of **Plug and Play** infrastructure, ensuring that industrial plots are equipped with all essential utilities like **water**, **power**, and **connectivity** up to the plot level, enabling immediate industrial activity. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• As a strategic **infrastructure initiative**, NICDP aims to revolutionize **urban and industrial development** in India, creating a global manufacturing hub and facilitating **planned urbanization**. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT)**:

 
 
• Function: It is the **apex body** under the administrative control of the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**.
 
• Mandatary: It oversees the **coordinated development** of all industrial corridors in the country.
 
 
 
• **Major Industrial Corridors**:
 
 
• **Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC)**: Focused on the **Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor**.
 
• **Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC)**: Aims to foster growth in **South India**, including extensions to **Kochi** via **Palakkad**.
 
• **Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)**: India’s first **coastal industrial corridor**, part of the **East Coast Economic Corridor**.

questions.question: Considering the periodic trends, which property explains why noble gases are chemically inert under standard conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Completely filled valence shell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Noble gases**, located in **Group 18** of the **Periodic Table**, are characterized by their extreme lack of chemical reactivity under **standard conditions**.
 
• The fundamental reason for this stability is their **electronic configuration**; they possess a **completely filled valence shell**, which corresponds to a total of eight electrons (the **octet rule**) for elements like **Neon**, **Argon**, **Krypton**, **Xenon**, and **Radon**.
 
• **Helium**, the lightest noble gas, has a **duplet** configuration (1s²), which is also a fully occupied and highly stable **valence shell**.
 
• An atom with a full valence shell is in its lowest energy state, meaning it has no energetic incentive to gain, lose, or share electrons with other atoms to form **chemical bonds**.
 
• Because these atoms do not easily form compounds, they exist as **monatomic gases** and are described as being **chemically inert** or **noble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ionization Energy**

 
 
• Noble gases have the **highest ionization energy** in their respective periods because their electrons are held very tightly by the **nucleus** within a stable shell.
 
• The statement **Low ionization energy** is incorrect, as low values would facilitate the removal of electrons, making an element highly reactive like the **alkali metals**.
 
 
 
• **Electronegativity**

• The flora consists of scattered trees and thorny bushes such as **Acacia**, **Palms**, **Euphorbias**, and various types of **Cacti**.
 
• Plants in this ecosystem have developed **xerophytic adaptations**, including long taproots that reach deep into the water table and **succulent stems** designed for moisture conservation.

• The dominant species is the **Sundari tree**, which provides durable timber and thrives in saline swampy conditions.
 
 
 
• **Malabar Coast**:
 
 
• Situated along the **Western Ghats**, this area receives heavy rainfall (above 250 cm) from the **Southwest Monsoon**.
 
• It is home to **Tropical Evergreen** and **Semi-Evergreen forests**, featuring species like **Rosewood**, **Mahogany**, and **Ebony**.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Himalayas**:

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India can issue how many types of writs (orders)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 32** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Supreme Court** is empowered to issue five types of writs for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** guaranteed by Part III.
 
• **Habeas Corpus**: Literally meaning 'to have the body of', this writ is issued to protect **personal liberty** against arbitrary detention by the state or private individuals.
 
• **Mandamus**: Translating to 'we command', it is a judicial order issued to a **public official**, lower court, or government body to perform a **statutory duty** that they have failed or refused to execute.
 
• **Prohibition**: This writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court or quasi-judicial body to **prevent** it from exceeding its jurisdiction or acting contrary to the rules of natural justice.
 
• **Certiorari**: Meaning 'to be certified', it is issued to **quash** an order already passed by an inferior court or tribunal when there is an error of law or a lack of jurisdiction.
 
• **Quo-Warranto**: Meaning 'by what authority', the court issues this to enquire into the **legality of a person's claim** to a public office, ensuring that no one usurps a public position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 32 and Article 226**

 
 
• **Article 32** is itself a **Fundamental Right**, which **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** famously described as the **Heart and Soul of the Constitution**.
 
• The **High Courts** also possess the power to issue these five writs under **Article 226** of the Constitution.
 
• The **writ jurisdiction** of the High Court is considered wider than that of the Supreme Court because High Courts can issue writs for both **Fundamental Rights** and **ordinary legal rights**.
 
• While the Supreme Court is the **guarantor** of Fundamental Rights, its writ jurisdiction is limited to Part III of the Constitution.
 
• The concept of writs in India is heavily influenced by **English Common Law**, specifically the **Prerogative Writs**.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance forms of India originated among the Kathakars (storytellers) of northern India, later incorporating elements of Bhakti traditions as well as Persian and Central Asian influences during the Mughal period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Kathak** is derived from the **Sanskrit** word **Katha**, meaning 'story', and **Kathakars** were traditional traveling storytellers who narrated **mythological** epics through dance, music, and song.
 
• This classical dance form originated in **Northern India**, primarily within the regions of **Uttar Pradesh** and **Rajasthan**, initially performed in village temples to depict devotional themes.
 
• During the 15th and 16th centuries, the **Bhakti movement** significantly influenced the dance, introducing themes of divine love centered around **Lord Krishna** and **Radha**.
 
• Under the **Mughal Empire**, **Kathak** shifted from temples to the royal courts, where it integrated **Persian** and **Central Asian** aesthetic elements, emphasizing technical virtuosity.
 
• Key technical features developed during the **Mughal period** include lightning-fast **Chakkars** (pirouettes), complex **Tatkar** (footwork), and the use of the **Angarkha** (costume).
 
• The dance is characterized by the use of **Ghungroos** (bells) and is categorized into major **Gharanas** or schools, namely **Lucknow**, **Jaipur**, and **Banaras**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kuchipudi**:

 
 
• Originated in **Andhra Pradesh**, this dance form combines **Lasya** and **Tandava** elements and was traditionally performed by male **Brahmins** in the village of **Kuchelapuram**.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**:
 
 
• Hailing from **Tamil Nadu**, it is the oldest classical dance of India, rooted in the **Sadir Attam** tradition of temple **Devadasis** and based on the principles of the **Natya Shastra**.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**:
 
 
• A graceful, feminine dance form from **Kerala**, it is named after **Mohini**, the celestial enchantress, and is known for its swaying movements and **circular** patterns.

questions.question: Which Article allows constitutional remedies for enforcement of Fundamental Rights by courts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**, making it possible for citizens to move the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
 
• This article is itself a **Fundamental Right** included in **Part III**, ensuring that the other rights guaranteed to citizens are not merely paper declarations but are legally enforceable.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the architect of the Constitution, described **Article 32** as the **'Heart and Soul'** of the Constitution, asserting that the entire constitutional structure would be meaningless without this provision.
 
• Under this article, the **Supreme Court** is empowered to issue five types of **Writs**: **Habeas Corpus** (to produce a body), **Mandamus** (we command), **Prohibition** (to stay proceedings), **Certiorari** (to quash orders), and **Quo Warranto** (by what authority).
 
• The **Supreme Court** has **Original Jurisdiction** under this article, meaning an aggrieved citizen can directly approach the highest court without following the hierarchical appeal process.
 
• The rights guaranteed by **Article 32** cannot be suspended except as provided by the Constitution, such as during a **National Emergency** under **Article 359**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 226**:

 
 
• Grants **High Courts** the power to issue writs for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights** and for **'any other purpose'**, which refers to ordinary legal rights.
 
• While the **Supreme Court's** jurisdiction is limited to **Fundamental Rights**, the **High Court's** jurisdiction under **Article 226** is actually broader in scope.
 
 
 
• **Article 44**:
 
 
• Contains the provision for a **Uniform Civil Code** (UCC) for all citizens throughout the territory of **India**.
 
• It is categorized under the **Directive Principles of State Policy** (DPSP) in **Part IV**, which are guidelines for the state but are not enforceable by courts.
 
 
 
• **Article 300**:
 
 
• Deals with **Suits and Proceedings** by or against the **Government of India** or the **State Governments** in their corporate capacity.
 
• Historically related is **Article 300A**, which was added by the **44th Amendment Act, 1978**, to establish the **Right to Property** as a **Constitutional Right** instead of a **Fundamental Right**.

questions.question: A computer’s characteristic of Accuracy means it can produce precise and correct results as long as the ________ is/are correct.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**input data and instructions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Accuracy** is a fundamental characteristic of a computer, referring to its ability to perform calculations and process data with 100% precision without making any internal errors.
 
• The accuracy of a computer depends entirely on the **GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out)** principle. This concept implies that the quality of the output is directly proportional to the quality of the **input data and instructions** provided by the user.
 
• Computers are **logical machines** that execute **algorithms** exactly as they are written; therefore, if the **input data** is incorrect or if the **program instructions** contain logical errors (bugs), the computer will produce a wrong result.
 
• Unlike humans, computers do not suffer from **fatigue**, boredom, or lack of concentration, which are common causes of human error. As long as the hardware is functioning correctly, errors in output are almost always traceable back to **human mistakes** in data entry or programming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resolution of the display screen**:

 
 
• Refers to the number of **pixels** (horizontal × vertical) that a screen can display.
 
• It determines the **visual clarity**, sharpness, and detail of the image but has no influence on the mathematical or logical **accuracy** of the computer's processing units.
 
 
 
• **Size of the system's RAM**:
 
 
• **Random Access Memory (RAM)** is the **volatile memory** used to store data currently being processed by the CPU.
 
• Increasing **RAM capacity** enhances **multitasking** capabilities and overall **system speed**, but it does not change the correctness of a calculation.
 
 
 
• **Speed of the processor**:
 
 
• Measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)**, it indicates how many **clock cycles** a CPU can perform per second.
 
• A faster **processor** allows for **high-speed execution** of tasks but does not improve the inherent **precision** of the logic applied to the data.

questions.question: Which molecule is primarily responsible for storing genetic information in most living organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)** is the primary molecule responsible for the long-term storage of **genetic information** in almost all living organisms, including plants, animals, and bacteria.
 
• The structure of DNA is a **double helix**, composed of two strands made of **deoxyribose sugar** and **phosphate groups**, famously modeled by **James Watson** and **Francis Crick** in **1953**.
 
• Genetic data is stored in the **nucleotide sequence** of four nitrogenous bases: **Adenine (A)**, **Thymine (T)**, **Cytosine (C)**, and **Guanine (G)**, where A always pairs with T and C always pairs with G via **hydrogen bonds**.
 
• In **eukaryotic organisms**, DNA is primarily housed within the **cell nucleus** in the form of **chromosomes**, though small amounts are also found in **mitochondria** and **chloroplasts**.
 
• The molecule is capable of **self-replication**, a critical process that ensures **hereditary information** is passed accurately from parent cells to daughter cells during **cell division**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RNA (Ribonucleic Acid)**:

 
 
• Generally single-stranded and contains the sugar **ribose** and the base **Uracil (U)** instead of Thymine.
 
• While it acts as the primary genetic material in some **viruses** (like retroviruses), its main role in most organisms is **protein synthesis** (translation).
 
 
 
• **Protein**:
 
 
• Large biomolecules consisting of **amino acids** that perform diverse cellular functions such as **enzymatic catalysis**, structural support, and signaling.
 
• They do not store genetic information but are the physical expression of the code stored in DNA.
 
 
 
• **Lipid**:
 
 
• Diverse group of **hydrophobic** molecules, including **fats** and **phospholipids**, primarily used for **energy storage** and forming the **cell membrane** bilayer.

questions.question: The Right to Information Act 2005 was extended to the whole of India except which of the following state/UT at the time of enactment in 2005?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005** was enacted by the **Parliament of India** to provide a practical regime for citizens to access information under the control of public authorities.
 
• At the time of its enactment and subsequent commencement on **October 12, 2005**, **Section 1(2)** of the Act specifically stated that it extended to the **whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• This exclusion was a result of the special autonomous status granted to **Jammu and Kashmir** under **Article 370** of the **Constitution of India**, which required the state government's concurrence for the application of central laws.
 
• Because the central law did not apply, the state government of **Jammu and Kashmir** implemented its own version, known as the **Jammu and Kashmir Right to Information Act, 2004**, which was later replaced by the **J&K RTI Act, 2009**.
 
• The act aims to promote **transparency** and **accountability** in the working of every public authority, helping to contain **corruption** and make democracy work for the people in a real sense.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legal Evolution and Reorganisation:**

 
 
• The legal landscape changed significantly with the passage of the **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019**, which led to the abrogation of **Article 370** and the reorganization of the state into two **Union Territories**.
 
• Effective from **October 31, 2019**, the central **RTI Act, 2005** became applicable to the **Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir** and the **Union Territory of Ladakh**, repealing the state-specific act.
 
• States like **Tripura**, **West Bengal**, and **Mizoram** were included in the original 2005 implementation as they did not have the constitutional exemption that J&K possessed at that time.
 
• The **RTI Act** replaced the previous **Freedom of Information Act, 2002**, providing a much stronger framework for the exercise of the **fundamental right** to information under **Article 19(1)** of the Constitution.

questions.question: In which year was the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) formed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1924**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Hindustan Republican Association (HRA)** was a revolutionary organization founded in **October 1924**.
 
• The founding meeting of the **HRA** took place in **Kanpur**, Uttar Pradesh, following the suspension of the **Non-Cooperation Movement** by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The primary objective of the association was to overthrow the **British colonial government** through an organized armed revolution and establish the **Federal Republic of the United States of India**.
 
• The organization was established by prominent revolutionaries including **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**, **Ram Prasad Bismil**, **Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee**, and **Ashfaqullah Khan**.
 
• The **HRA** drafted a constitution and a manifesto titled **'The Revolutionary'**, which outlined their vision for a democratic India based on **universal adult suffrage** and the abolition of exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of the Organization**:

 
 
• **Kakori Conspiracy (1925)**: On **August 9, 1925**, HRA members carried out the famous **Kakori train robbery** to fund their revolutionary activities, which led to a massive crackdown by the British.
 
• **Formation of HSRA (1928)**: After the arrest of several **HRA** leaders, the organization was reorganized as the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)** at **Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi**, in **September 1928**.
 
• **Influence of Socialism**: Under the influence of **Bhagat Singh** and **Chandrashekhar Azad**, the **HSRA** formally adopted **socialism** as its core ideology to address social and economic inequalities.
 
• **Key Figures**: While **Sachindra Nath Sanyal** authored the influential book **Bandi Jeevan**, **Chandrashekhar Azad** served as the **Commander-in-Chief** of the reorganized association.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AYUSH Systems of Medicine**:

• **Yoga and Naturopathy**: Focuses on **drug-less** healing through physical postures, meditation, and **hydrotherapy**.
 
• **Unani, Siddha, and Homoeopathy**: Other recognized components of the **AYUSH** framework that utilize natural substances and personalized treatment protocols.
 
 
 
• **Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS)**:

• **Allopathic treatment**: The **modern pharmacological** system of medicine that uses **synthetic drugs** and surgical interventions to treat symptoms.
 
• **Advanced cardiac treatment**: High-end medical procedures for **heart diseases**, including **cardiology** diagnostics and **cardiothoracic surgery**.
 
 
 
• **Patanjali Yoggram**:
 
 
• Located in **Haridwar**, it is a flagship center for **integrated healthcare**, established by **Baba Ramdev** and **Acharya Balkrishna**.
